name: UCWF World Championship
notes: Billed once as the “Heavyweight Championship” at Wrestle Insanity's own finish (promotions/ucwf/archive/wrestle-insanity-2003.html); every other appearance calls it the World Championship.
epitaph: UCWF's own top title changed hands six times across the surviving record, twice on the strength of a bare rollup rather than a clean finish: Johnny Johnson loses it to Bobby Linken at Wrestle Insanity while distracted by a fabricated news report naming him alongside a dying convicted murderer, and The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni takes it from Johnson at Resurrection on a quick count by special guest referee Mumrat, the fed's own owner. Giovanni's own reign is the longest the record shows in outline: he survives a 60-minute Hell In A Cell Ironman against Ace Of Spades at Fury 2003-06-20, three falls to two, only to lose the belt to the same man weeks later in a Breakout dome-cage match, kicked off a 20-foot ladder short of the roof hatch Ace pulls himself through alone. Ace Of Spades is the last champion the surviving record shows.

name: UCWF Universal Championship
epitaph: The record's own account of this belt opens on a finish nobody could call: Ace Of Spades and challenger Jinx both have their shoulders down for referee Gangsta Mac's own three-count at Immortality 2002, and the announce team simply refuses to name a winner. The lineage that follows is a chain of retains broken by unrecorded turnovers — CM2, The Krazy Kid and Mr. Wacko each hold it into a show where the record shows someone else already champion — until “QBz Finest” Blaze takes it from Wacko at Resurrection and The Fox wins it off Blaze in a six-man Six Pack Challenge at Breakout, the last title change the surviving record shows for this belt.

name: UCWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The Krazy-Wacko Connection is this belt's own constant, winning and losing it three separate times across the surviving record without ever being shown regaining it on-page: from Dark Carnival at Immortality 2002, lost by disqualification to The G's at Fury 2002-09-08 days later, regained unrecorded by Wrestle Insanity only to lose it there to A.C.E. (Ace Of Spades and Crash Paradise), then regained again unrecorded in time to defend it, “STILL” champions, against Italian Organized Crime at Resurrection — the last the surviving record shows of the belt.

name: UCWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: Scorpion, of the stable American Bad Boyz, opens the surviving record's own account of this title by taking it from Crash Paradise at Immortality 2002 and defending it at Fury 2002-09-08 — Johnny Johnson steals the belt off him afterward with a kendo stick, an angle beat the record never turns into an actual title change. The lineage that follows shows three more unrecorded turnovers before landing on Notorious, then “QBz Finest” Blaze, who takes it from him at Wrestle Insanity, then “The Reality” A.J. Simmons, who loses it to Rich Bitch at Resurrection — the last champion the surviving record shows.

name: UCWF Extreme Championship
epitaph: A hardcore-stipulation title from the start — a Thumbtacks Match, a Flaming Hell In A Cell, a Deathmatch, a Barbwire Beat Down — that “QBz Finest” Blaze loses to Wes Easton in the first of those at Fury 2002-09-08. Flashing Thunder holds it through an unrecorded turnover into a draw against The Fox at Wrestle Insanity, then loses it, also unrecorded, to Kevin Murray by the time Bryon Wade Osbourne makes his own UCWF debut at Fury 2003-06-20 and wins the title in a Deathmatch with his first opponent. Osbourne survives a draw against Sean Johnson (and a mid-match elimination of Flashing Thunder) at Breakout — the last the surviving record shows of the belt.

name: UCWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Mr. Wacko takes this title from The Fox at Immortality 2002 with a backslide and defends it days later at Fury 2002-09-08 in a fatal four-way against Crazy Hayze, Bobby Linken and Crusher — the last the surviving record shows of the belt, Wacko still champion when the record ends.

name: UCWF Vamped Championship
epitaph: Absent from the fed's own two 2002 shows, first attested with The Krazy Kid already champion at Wrestle Insanity. The Fox takes it from him at Resurrection, loses it to “Prime Time” The Vine at Fury 2003-06-20, and Vine — billed at Breakout as having “just won the title last week” — retains it there against Santa Claus, the last the surviving record shows of the belt.

name: UCWF International Championship
epitaph: A tournament for a third singles title, its own bracket shown only in first-round action at Fury 2003-06-20: Mr. Wacko advances past Jason Compton and Bobby Linken, and The Krazy Kid advances past Santa Claus. No further round survives in the record, and no champion is ever named.
